title: SVG Thumbnails not showing as thumbnails.

judgment.rationale: The issue remains open; the 2026-06 reporter says Windows color mode changes SVG thumbnail visibility. The 2026-10-19 SageThumbs recommendation is a disclosed third-party workaround, not a PowerToys fix. The renderer-background hypothesis is plausible but unconfirmed.
evidence: Original report: PowerToys 0.60.0 displayed an Edge icon instead of an SVG thumbnail; screenshots and a diagnostic ZIP were attached.
A 2025 reporter confirmed persistence on PowerToys 0.89.0.
A 2026 reporter says light/dark Windows color mode changes the SVG thumbnail background and can hide dark artwork.
A 2026-10-19 commenter recommends SageThumbs and discloses being its author.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a focused design investigation that confirms thumbnail provider behavior across Windows themes.

fix_assessment.rationale: A repository-side change is plausible, but the current causal hypothesis requires verification.

proposed_fixes.title: Keep SVG thumbnail artwork visible across Windows themes
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: the thumbnail provider uses a theme-dependent canvas that can blend with or obscure dark artwork; the thread does not show that this explains icon-fallback cases.

confidence.rationale: The recent report isolates a theme-dependent symptom, but the thread also includes unrelated icon-fallback cases and no source trace confirms one cause.

verification: Compare identical dark and light SVG samples in Windows light and dark modes, including after clearing Explorer thumbnail cache.
Confirm the SVG preview pane and existing provider fallback behavior remain unchanged.
plan: Trace SVG thumbnail background and theme selection in light and dark modes.
Separate provider failures returning an Edge icon from successful renders with low-contrast artwork.
If confirmed, use a stable transparent/contrast policy and add tests for dark and light SVG samples.

issue_context.summary: Multiple reports describe incorrect or invisible SVG thumbnails; the latest maintainer-relevant clue associates visibility with Windows color mode, while a third-party extension is only a workaround.
known_information: Original report: PowerToys 0.60.0 displayed an Edge icon instead of an SVG thumbnail; screenshots and a diagnostic ZIP were attached.
A 2025 reporter confirmed persistence on PowerToys 0.89.0.
A 2026 reporter says light/dark Windows color mode changes the SVG thumbnail background and can hide dark artwork.
A 2026-10-19 commenter recommends SageThumbs and discloses being its author.
inferences: A theme-dependent thumbnail background may hide otherwise-rendered artwork, but this does not explain all Edge-icon or blank-thumbnail reports.
The third-party extension is a workaround and does not establish that PowerToys is fixed.
issue_context.analysis: The issue remains actionable. The recent theme clue needs verification against the thumbnail provider before selecting a fix, and no third-party workaround should be treated as resolution.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the complete live body, 20 comments, labels, and linked SVG issue family.
No current PowerToys PR or owner-backed fix was identified.

actions.description: Approve a focused design investigation that confirms thumbnail provider behavior across Windows themes.
actions.label: Approve SVG thumbnail design

prerequisites: Use a dark-artwork SVG and a light-artwork SVG.
Compare Windows light/dark color modes and clear Explorer thumbnail cache between comparisons.
steps: Enable the PowerToys SVG thumbnail provider.
Compare the same files as Explorer thumbnails in Windows light mode and note artwork visibility versus Edge icon fallback.
Repeat in dark mode and after refreshing the thumbnail cache.
Compare with the SVG preview pane.
reproduce.expected_result: SVG artwork remains distinguishable in both Windows color modes; provider failures are distinguishable from contrast issues.
